A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from DebiasDiff to FairGen. All pages, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections are readable and support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original gender, racial and intersectional debiasing experiments, cross-model transfer results, ablations and generated-image examples, including supplementary visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds ITI-GEN comparisons, training and inference measurements, and experiments combining four sensitive attributes.

M1.justification: The attribute adapters, noise-composition objective, distribution-indicator inference and orthogonal regularization remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.4. Renaming the method and evaluating additional attributes do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Appendix 10 and Table 8 extend evaluation beyond gender and race to age and body type, including three- and four-attribute combinations. This substantially broadens the demographic attributes and joint debiasing requirements actually evaluated. Existing occupation-based coverage is retained.

E2.justification: ITI-GEN is added to the gender, racial and intersectional comparisons in Tables 1, 2 and 4. Original SD, F4Fair, H Guidance, UCE and InterDiff remain in those comparisons. This is a limited expansion of the comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported guidance settings from eta = alpha = 1 to 0.3, although v2 Appendix 7 still states 1. This establishes a reporting change, not that experiments were rerun. The principal sampling and training budgets remain unchanged; new appendix evaluations add timing measurements and FID.

E4.justification: New Appendix 10 adds computational-efficiency comparisons and a progressive one-to-four-attribute scalability analysis in Tables 7–8. These examine practical cost and performance as attribute combinations expand, substantially extending the analyses. Existing transferability, adapter-location and orthogonal-regularization studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries in Tables 1–6 are unchanged, but ITI-GEN result rows are added. Tables 7–8 introduce substantial new efficiency and scalability results: FairGen reports 1.0-hour training and 6.2-second inference, while scalability FD ranges from 0.041 to 0.045. These are newly reported results, not demonstrated same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix 10 adds an explicit O(kc) adapter-count statement for k attributes with c categories each. This is a limited complexity analysis; the existing mathematical definitions, Equations (1)–(12) and noise-guidance derivation remain unchanged, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive contributions: self-discovered attribute directions, no reference-dataset dependence, lightweight transferable adapters, prescribed distributions and superior debiasing performance. The new experiments support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Appendix 10 newly explains scalability through modular adapters and selective activation. It also qualifies the role of orthogonality by stating that strict orthogonality is not essential and proposing selective regularization as future work. This changes the interpretation without documenting an implemented method revision.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies a single A100 GPU and training within 0.5 hours per adapter. Conversely, it removes v1's promised code-release link without replacement. The conflicting guidance settings in Sections 5.1 and 7 also reduce implementation clarity; actual external code availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds ITI-GEN as reference 37 and expands discussion of reference-image-based prompting. It also refines training-versus-retraining descriptions, including correcting F4Fair's appendix classification. However, Appendix 8 cites ITI-GEN as reference 36, which the bibliography identifies as Inclusive GAN.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and the method renamed FairGen; author affiliations and acknowledgements are updated. There are localized introduction rewrites, terminology corrections and a new scalability appendix section. Most prose and the existing section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 7–8 are added, and Tables 1, 2 and 4 gain ITI-GEN rows. Existing tables are resized or restyled, captions receive edits, and supplementary figures are repositioned to accommodate text. Figures 1–12 retain their underlying examples and findings.

improvement.justification: ITI-GEN comparisons and Tables 7–8 broaden empirical support for fairness, efficiency and scalability. However, v1's consistent guidance setting becomes contradictory in v2: Section 5.1 states 0.3 while Appendix 7 retains 1. The code-release link disappears, and the new age/body-type evaluation and FID results lack classifier and reference-data details. These benefits and reproducibility drawbacks leave the net quality change uncertain.
